new_statements.quote: Nahuat exhibits the following phonemes: consonants /p, t, k, b, d, g, m, n, c, č, kʷ, s, š, h, l, w, y/; vowels /i, e, a, o/; suprasegmental phonemes /:/ (vowel augment) and /'/ (stress). [...] Stress is unmarked when it occurs on the penult of the word unit; it is marked by an acute accent when it occurs on a different syllable of the word. (p. 108-109) [...] proclitics are bound particles which occur preceding the verb root and its affixes, which when combined with a verb construction do not shift the stress [...]; enclitics are bound particles which occur following the word, which when combined with a verb construction do not shift the stress (p. 122)

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog rule (penultimate stress = penultimate). Adds that non-penult stress exists as a marked minority and that clitics are outside the stress domain.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is phonemic in the analysis but falls by default on the penultimate syllable of the word unit; only words stressed elsewhere are marked with an acute accent. Proclitics and enclitics attach without moving the stress, so the penult is counted in the host word, not in the clitic group.
new_statements.exceptions: Words with stress on a syllable other than the penult exist and are marked with an acute accent; no list or rule for them is given. Clitics do not shift stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Law 1958 describes the forms heard in the municipio of Mecayapan, Ver. (p. 108: 'The village of Mecayapan, Ver., is one of a dozen or so where this dialect is spoken, and is the municipio of the area where the forms described in this paper are heard'). Wolgemuth 2002 covers the municipios of Mecayapan and Tatahuicapan de Juárez (Tatahuicapan was split off from Mecayapan after the 1981 first edition, preface p. ix) and says the variety is very close to Pajapan Nahuatl (p. xiii). Works 2 and 3 are one work (two landing pages for the same PDF, 2nd electronic edition, Oct. 2002 rev. Dec. 2002). The WALS refdb record for Law 1958 gives the volume as 22; the issue itself and CrossRef give vol. 24.

new_statements.quote: 1.5.2. Palabras agudas. Son aquellas en las cuales la última sílaba se pronuncia con mayor intensidad. Ejemplos: ahuel no se puede, ijquïn de esta manera, ijcõn de esa manera, nicpiá lo tengo, nicpiáj lo tenemos, sejsÿ sejsÿ uno por uno. Palabras agudas por proceso de contracción incluyen: quité¬ lo cortó, quimá¬ lo dio. 1.5.3. Palabras graves. Son aquellas en las que la penúltima sílaba se pronuncia con mayor intensidad. Los siguientes ejemplos se escriben sin acento ortográfico: imâ su mano [...] 1.5.4. Palabras esdrújulas. Son aquellas en las que la sílaba de mayor intensidad está en el lugar anterior al penúltimo [...] [n. 7:] Todos los ejemplos de palabras esdrújulas y sobresdrújulas llevan pospuestas una o más partículas de tipo enclítico. (pp. 11-12)
new_statements.translation: 1.5.2. Oxytone words. Those in which the last syllable is pronounced with greater intensity. Examples: ahuel 'cannot', ijquïn 'in this way', ijcõn 'in that way', nicpiá 'I have it', nicpiáj 'we have it', sejsÿ sejsÿ 'one by one'. Oxytones produced by contraction include: quité¬ 'he cut it', quimá¬ 'he gave it'. 1.5.3. Paroxytone words. Those in which the penultimate syllable is pronounced with greater intensity. The following examples are written without an orthographic accent: imâ 'his/her hand' [...] 1.5.4. Proparoxytone words. Those in which the syllable of greatest intensity is in the position before the penult [...] [n. 7:] All the examples of proparoxytone and pre-proparoxytone words carry one or more postposed enclitic-type particles. (pp. 11-12) [Note: in the extracted text output the underline marking long vowels renders as circumflex/diaeresis-like glyphs, e.g. imâ, ijquïn, and the saltillo apostrophe as ¬.]

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog (penult) and adds the exceptions: lexical oxytones, contracted verb forms with final stress, and stress domain excluding enclitics (so surface antepenult stress = penult of the host).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress ('acento prosódico', 'mayor intensidad') falls on the penultimate syllable as the normal case ('palabra grave.. como es normal', p. 160). Final stress occurs in a small set of words (ahuel, ijquïn, ijcõn, nicpiá, nicpiáj, sejsÿ) and in contracted verb forms; antepenult and pre-antepenult stress arise only when one or more enclitic particles are added to a penult-stressed word, i.e. the stress is computed on the host word and clitics do not count.
new_statements.exceptions: Oxytones: a short list of lexical items plus 'contract' verb variants where the final syllable is dropped without stress shift (p. 160). Proparoxytones/pre-proparoxytones: all due to enclitic particles (fn. 7, p. 12; §16.10 p. 139). The orthographic accent rules (§1.5.1) are conditioned on final l/r, but that is orthography, not stress placement.
new_statements.identity_note: Law 1958 describes the forms heard in the municipio of Mecayapan, Ver. (p. 108: 'The village of Mecayapan, Ver., is one of a dozen or so where this dialect is spoken, and is the municipio of the area where the forms described in this paper are heard'). Wolgemuth 2002 covers the municipios of Mecayapan and Tatahuicapan de Juárez (Tatahuicapan was split off from Mecayapan after the 1981 first edition, preface p. ix) and says the variety is very close to Pajapan Nahuatl (p. xiii). Works 2 and 3 are one work (two landing pages for the same PDF, 2nd electronic edition, Oct. 2002 rev. Dec. 2002). The WALS refdb record for Law 1958 gives the volume as 22; the issue itself and CrossRef give vol. 24.

new_statements.quote: Hay un conjunto de partículas, o sea terminaciones, adverbiales monosílabas que van pospuestas a los verbos, los adjetivos, los adverbios, y aun a las palabras sustantivas, sin causar cambio en la posición del acento prosódico. Es decir, al agregarle a la palabra una partícula enclítica, el acento prosódico queda en la misma sílaba. Resulta que la palabra grave se convierte en esdrújula al agregarle una partícula enclítica. Y al agregarle dos o más partículas, la palabra se convierte en sobresdrújula. (Véase la sección 1.5.) (p. 139) [...] con el resultado de que la palabra permanece grave, es decir la sílaba tónica queda penúltima, como es normal. (p. 160)
new_statements.translation: There is a set of monosyllabic adverbial particles, i.e. endings, that are postposed to verbs, adjectives, adverbs and even nouns without causing any change in the position of the prosodic stress. That is, when an enclitic particle is added to the word, the prosodic stress stays on the same syllable. The result is that a paroxytone word becomes a proparoxytone when an enclitic particle is added, and when two or more particles are added the word becomes pre-proparoxytone. (See section 1.5.) (p. 139) [...] with the result that the word remains paroxytone, that is, the stressed syllable stays penultimate, as is normal. (p. 160)

new_statements.rule_in_words: Same work as index 2 (the two Glottolog entries are the Spanish and the -NAU landing pages of one PDF). Penultimate stress is the norm; enclitic particles are outside the stress domain, so adding them yields surface antepenult or earlier stress without any shift; apocopated verb forms re-stress to keep the penult, while 'contract' forms keep the old stress and become oxytone.
new_statements.exceptions: Enclitic-bearing words (surface esdrújulas/sobresdrújulas); contract verb variants with final stress; small set of lexical oxytones (§1.5.2).

audit.reasoning: Quote check: every deciding passage (sec. 18.2 p. 160 default-penult statement; sec. 1.5.2-1.5.5 pp. 11-13 accent classes with fn. 7; sec. 16.10 p. 139 enclitic non-shift) is verbatim in the extracted text we hold of Wolgemuth 2002 at the cited locators. The source is the language's reference grammar (2nd ed. of the 1981 SIL grammar, Glottolog's top grammar entry), so the classification — penultimate default, non-strict, exceptions = a short closed list of oxytones plus contracted preterites, antepenult/pre-antepenult only via stress-neutral enclitics — rests on the best available description and is internally consistent across three sections of it. The earlier 'lexical' quick-screen reading is explained by the Spanish-style agudas/graves/esdrújulas presentation in sec. 1.5, which fn. 7 and sec. 16.10/18.2 resolve as derived classes.
